propositions: Build and validate a committed Git history rewrite script using stock plumbing (fast-export/fast-import with byte-length-aware filter) that strips .bridge_state/ and .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ from all historical revisions while preserving DAG topology, merge structure, and empty commits.

Dry-run script must refuse to execute in partial clones (blob:none), require fresh unfiltered checkout with --no-tags, assert dynamic bridge-state files via ls-tree, and prove old-tip tree byte-identical to rewritten-tip tree after dynamic re-add.

Script must correctly parse fast-export data blocks by byte length (not line-based grep) to handle commit messages beginning with M or D, and must preserve all commit and merge counts and history structure through the rewrite.

Dry-run script performs no remote push, leaves source refs (tickets branch and pre-heal tag) unchanged, measures rewritten pack ≤150 MB, and completes all graph/tree/history/tag assertions before emitting success.
After rewrite, representative review-bot event push must succeed with <1 MiB incremental pack and old-tip must not be ancestor of new-tip, confirming forward-only history.
All 17 acceptance criteria verified via unit stream-filter tests and real-repository integration tests; all gates (lint, typecheck, test) pass; no production push occurs during dry run.
